narrative_md:
## Audit summary (illustrative example)

Baseline for the third-floor suite: 308,797 kWh of electricity and 1,526 kWh of gas a year, about $92,784 (range $72,178 to $107,739). Electricity is on LADWP with net metering, priced at the EIA California commercial average rather than a LADWP schedule; gas is priced at the EIA California commercial average too. Office hot water is not modelled. The figures are simulated on the example weather year, not the site's own typical-year file, so they will move when that file is present. No bills were given, so the model is not calibrated to bills and every saving below is an uncalibrated estimate. The modelled gas use is low against surveyed offices of this size, and the benchmark asks for a check of the model before relying on it.

The plan follows a consultant's loading order: operations first, then load reduction, then equipment, and solar last, sized against the electricity that is left. Within each step the most cost-effective measure goes first, and a measure is recommended only if its savings-to-investment ratio (SIR) is at least 1. Within the $150,000 budget it selects, in that order, desk placement (no cost, saving about $364 a year) and rooftop solar ($149,812, saving about $20,828 a year): $149,812 upfront, saving about $21,192 a year (range $19,002 to $23,382).

Solar comes last and is shrunk to the budget that is left. Filled to the suite's annual use, the flat roof of about 2,567 m2 would carry 199.09 kW (SIR 2.93); the plan takes 44.72 kW on racks for $149,812, which may exceed the budget at the high end of its cost range. It pays back in about 7.8 years on its own (SIR 1.92); the federal investment credit is not counted until its conditions are confirmed. The roof is mid-life, so a structural check and the roof's remaining life come before racking goes on.

Rooftop unit replacement, lighting controls and window replacement cost more over their life than they save (SIR below 1), so they are neither recommended nor offered for financing. Nothing is financeable, so no C-PACE view is put forward; any C-PACE scenario here would be hypothetical anyway, since no programme taking commercial applications in Los Angeles has been confirmed.

LED lighting and shades are already in place; a smart thermostat, air sealing and an economizer save nothing in the model; plug-load management and window film have no verified cost and need a quote. The LED lighting and the interior blinds came with the 2024 renovation, so neither is proposed again. The suite has a floor above it, so roof insulation and a cool roof do not apply to it.

Aerial captures disagree about the roof: an older capture outlines a much larger roof than the structure that matches CoStar's floor plate, which the design uses. Both show no solar today.

Value uplift: capitalised at the rates of 12 comparable sales, the plan's savings correspond to about $163,553 of property value (range $0 to $507,364). This is an estimate shown beside the totals; it is not added to the savings.
